scope: Separate NIintegrate arithmetic precision from linear-solve precision and binary64 state storage
interpretation: The kernel agrees with independent Decimal arithmetic across supported trapezoidal/Gear orders and cancellation controls. The actual NIintegrate adapter passes enabled, disabled and invalid-mode checks. With both experimental precision modes off, the rebuilt runtime reproduces all four baseline waveform hashes and the same timestep rejection. With higher-precision integration and the original linear solver, the replay still fails near the original transition. The trajectory changes, but integration arithmetic alone does not remedy the failure. The final audited inductor derivatives match correctly rounded exact logged-history arithmetic; substantial componentwise linear residuals remain with the original solver, followed by flux-history truncation rejection after Newton convergence. Internal and saved voltages in failed replays are not physical predictions. Combined high-precision integration and linear solving also fails near the same transition. The final audited inductor derivatives match correctly rounded exact logged-history arithmetic, and selected linear systems have small componentwise backward errors, yet large internal trial states and truncation rejection persist. Accurate local arithmetic does not establish an accurate accumulated trajectory or identify a unique failure cause.
boundary: Only per-call integration arithmetic changes. State history, time, integration coefficients, nonlinear evaluation and other device stamping remain binary64. Exact arithmetic on already-rounded history is not higher-precision history storage. Circuit physics and tolerance budgets remain unchanged. This analog-only replay cannot qualify firmware or physical behavior.
nextAction: Locate the onset of trajectory divergence in accepted and rejected state history; distinguish accumulated state, nonlinear evaluation and stamping sensitivity before choosing another numerical intervention. Require timestep refinement for any completed capture.
